'''Emanuele Foà''' (16 August 1892<ref name="birthdate" /> – 9 October 1949) was an Italian [[engineer]] and [[Engineering physics|engineering physicist]], known for his contribution to [[Fluid dynamics|mathematical fluid dynamics]]. In particular he proved the first known uniqueness theorem for the solutions to the [[Dimension (mathematics)|three-dimensional]] [[Navier–Stokes equations]] for incompressible fluids in [[bounded set|bounded]] [[Domain (mathematical analysis)|domains]].<ref>{{harv|Serrin|1959|loc=p. 251, footnote 1}}.</ref>

==Life and academic career==
He was born in Savigliano, in a Jewish family of distinguished professionals and officials:<ref name="Codp443" >{{harv|Codegone|1949|p=443}}.</ref> his father, Teodoro Foà, was a [[military physician]] serving as a [[Major (rank)|major]] the [[Royal Italian Army]],<ref name="50-158-443">See {{harv|Graffi|1949–1950|p=50}}, {{harv|Dore|1952|p=158}} and {{harv|Codegone|1949|p=443}}.</ref> who died at the age of 42 due to the [[viral fever]]s he contracted during the [[Italian Eritrea|Eritrea war campaign]].<ref name="Codp443" /> Despite having lost his father at a young age and having a disabled sister,<ref name="Zan.90">{{harv|Zanobetti|2002|p=90}}.</ref> he succeeded in studying engineering at the [[Polytechnic University of Turin]] thanks to a scholarship.<ref>According to {{harvtxt|Graffi|1949–1950|p=50}}.</ref> The outbreak of [[World War I]] in Italy in 1915 forced him to interrupt his engineering studies: he joined the army and served as an [[artillery]] [[Officer (armed forces)|officer]] for the years 1916 and 1917. On 28 October 1917, during the [[battle of Caporetto]], he was taken prisoner and spent a year in a [[prisoner-of-war camp|prisoner camp]] located in Germany.<ref name="50-158-443" /><ref>According to {{harvtxt|Dore|1952|p=158}}, the harshness of the camp conditions seriously undermined his health.</ref>

At the end of the war, notwithstanding his health problems, he successfully completed his university studies: he got his [[Laurea]] degree in [[industrial engineering]] at the Polytechnic University of Turin in August 1919.<ref>According to {{harvtxt|Codegone|1949|p=443}} and {{harvtxt|Graffi|1949–1950|p=50}}: {{harvtxt|Dore|1952|p=158}} gives only the basic information.</ref> From 1 December 1919 he started to work at his [[alma mater]],<ref>According to {{harvtxt|Codegone|1949|p=443}}: {{harvtxt|Graffi|1949–1950|p=50}} writes that he started on an unspecified day of November 1919.</ref> as [[assistant professor]] to the chair of thermal engineering,<ref>Precisely, to the chair of "''Termotecnica''" {{harv|Codegone|1949|p=443}}, {{harv|Graffi|1949–1950|p=50}}.</ref> which at the time was held by Benedetto Luigi Montel.<ref name="advsr" /> In 1927 he participated and won a competitive examination for a professorship in engineering physics at the then called "Royal School of Engineering of Bologna":<ref>As reported by {{harvs|txt|last=Codegone|year=1949|year2=1970|loc=p. 443|loc2=p. 34 and Ref. [28]}}.</ref> in 1928 he left Turin for Bologna,<ref>See {{harv|Garelli|1929|p=12}}, {{harv|Dore|1952|p=158}} and {{harv|Graffi|1949–1950|p=51}}. {{harvtxt|Graffi|1949–1950|p=51}} also says that Foà held the chair from January 1928.</ref> succeeding, after a brief time period, to [[Luigi Donati]] who had held the chair for several decades.<ref>According to {{harvtxt|Dore|1952|p=158}}. Also {{harvtxt|Zanobetti|2002|p=90}} briefly mentions this detail.</ref> The very same year he met Dario Graffi, who had earlier become assistant professor to the chair of engineering physics:<ref>As recalled by {{harvtxt|Graffi|1949–1950|p=46}} himself.</ref> their cordial relations became over time a deep and tenacious friendship, lasted until Foà's death.<ref>In the exact words of {{harvtxt|Graffi|1949–1950|pp=46–47}}, "''Subito, per Sua cortesia, si stabilì tra me e lui quella cordialità di rapporti che più tardi doveva mutarsi in profonda e tenace amicizia''" (English translation: "Immediately, for His kindness, that cordiality of relations between him and me that later had to change into a deep and tenacious friendship was established"). Also, {{harvtxt|Zanobetti|2002|p=90}} recalls their friendship and mutual respect briefly.</ref>

In Bologna, he passionately devoted himself to teaching as his course handouts, published in several editions, testify:<ref>According to {{harvtxt|Graffi|1949–1950|p=51}}: see also the "[[Emanuele Foà#Teaching activity|Teaching activity]]" section of this entry.</ref> the same time was fruitful for his researches activity,<ref>According to {{harvtxt|Codegone|1949|p=443}}: see also the "[[Emanuele Foà#Research activity|Research activity]]" section of this entry.</ref> and in 1930 he was appointed [[ordinary professor]].<ref name="Zan.90"/>

===The years from 1938 to 1945: the "Italian Racial Laws" and World War II===
His teaching at the university was interrupted in 1938, the year the Italian Government approved the "[[Italian Racial Laws|Racial Laws]]", "unreasonable, before being unjust".<ref>This sentence is reported by both {{harvtxt|Codegone|1949|p=444}} and {{harvtxt|Graffi|1949–1950|p=51}}: this latter one further remarks "''... come fu detto ottimamente, ...''" (English translation: "... as it was well said, ...").</ref> Forced by the law to an early [[retirement]], the [[Council]] of the faculty of engineering substituted him with Graffi: he was very happy with the council choice,<ref name="Zan.90" /> due to their friendship and mutual esteem.<ref>{{harvtxt|Graffi|1949–1950|p=46}}, {{harv|Zanobetti|2002|p=90}}.</ref> For his part, Graffi, who could not adopt Foà's handouts due to prohibition imposed by the laws on publications by Jewish authors, published them under his name:<ref name="Zan.90" /> cautiously, he kept sending to Foà's house students for private lessons, in order to help him supplement his small retirement pension.<ref>{{harvtxt|Zanobetti|2002|p=90}} describes in detail the life of Foà and his family during this period: {{harvtxt|Graffi|1949–1950|p=51}} and {{harvtxt|Codegone|1949|p=444}} mention briefly the private lessons he gave to students coming to his house.</ref>

During the [[World War II]] period, Foà and his wife managed to stay in Bologna but had to change their accommodation frequently, being hosted by friendly families.<ref>{{harv|Graffi|1949–1950|p=51}}, {{harvtxt|Codegone|1949|p=444}}.</ref> In October 1943, being warned by Dino Zanobetti about a raid of the police, he and his wife left their house and went to an apartment made available by Dante Piccioli, a wealthy engineer and friend of theirs.<ref>Zanobetti met Foà after being informed via a phone call by Graffi that he was still in Bologna: the episode is narrated in detail in {{harv|Zanobetti|2002|p=91}}.</ref> More than a month later, on 7 December, Bologna was bombed and the apartment where Foà and his wife resided was destroyed:<ref>{{harv|Zanobetti|2002|p=91}}.</ref> being at home,<ref>They did not go to the [[Bomb shelter#Air-raid shelter|air-raid shelters]], as {{harvtxt|Zanobetti|2002|p=91}} remarks, because they did not want to risk of being recognized, [[arrest]]ed and [[deportation|deported]].</ref> Foà was severely wounded in the right leg and was brought to the [[Policlinico Sant'Orsola-Malpighi|Sant'Orsola Hospital]].<ref>Following {{harvtxt|Zanobetti|2002|p=91}}. {{harvtxt|Graffi|1949–1950|p=51}} and {{harvtxt|Codegone|1949|p=444}} write very briefly of Foà's wounded leg and also give a different version, postponing the event in January 1944.</ref>

===Honours===
In 1933, he was elected [[corresponding member]] of the [[Accademia delle Scienze dell'Istituto di Bologna]]<ref>{{harv|Graffi|1949–1950|p=51}}</ref> and, after being reintegrated in his role of professor at the [[University of Bologna]] in 1945,<ref name="Cod444">See {{harv|Codegone|1949|p=444}}.</ref> he became ordinary member in 1947.<ref>According to {{harvtxt|Codegone|1949|p=444}} and {{harvtxt|Graffi|1949–1950|p=51}}, who states also the year of his election. Precisely, he became "''Accademico Benedettino''", i.e. literally "[[Pope Benedict XIV|Benedictine]] [[Academician]]", as this is the way every ordinary member of the Academy of Sciences of the Institute of Bologna is called.</ref> Also in 1947, jointly with some fellow engineers, he founded the Bologna Section of the Associazione Termotecnica Italiana,<ref name="Cod444" /><ref> the professional society of Italian [[Thermal engineering|thermal engineer]]s;</ref> he was elected as his first president.<ref name="Cod444" />

==Work==
===Teaching activity===
{{quote
|text=Si dedicò all'insegnamento con grande passione, lo provano i suoi corsi di dispense di cui si fecero diverse edizioni e in cui si manifesta la sua personalità didattica ad un tempo profonda e semplificatrice.<ref>(English translation) "''He devoted himself to teaching with great passion, and this is proved by its courses handouts which had several editions and which show his teaching personality, at once profound and simplifying.''"</ref>
|sign=[[Dario Graffi]]
|source={{harv|Graffi|1949–1950|p=51}}
}}

===Research activity===
{{quote
|text=Al primo periodo bolognese del Foà sono soprattutto da ascriversi le importanti ricerche sull'analisi dimensionale e sulle sue applicazioni allo studio dei processi tecnici in vista di dedurre, da tali analisi, metodi semplici e sicuri per stabilire importanti proprietà delle equazioni differenziali che tali processi reggono, pur senza integrarle.<ref>(English translation) "''To the first Bolognese period of Foà are to be ascribed important researches on [[dimensional analysis]] and its applications to the study of technical processes aimed to deduce, from such analyses, simple and safe methods to establish important properties of the [[Partial differential equation|differential equations]] governing such processes, though not [[Closed-form expression#Analytic expression|integrating]] them.''"</ref>
|sign= [[Paolo Dore]]
|source={{Harv|Dore|1952|p=158}}
}}
